rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Tables 2, 5-7, Figs. 2-7 - the authors report their own ten-year field experiment (2010-19) in a Sicilian orange orchard comparing full irrigation with sustained deficit, regulated deficit and partial root-zone drying treatments, with own measurements of stem water potential, sap flow, soil water content, yield, fruit quality and water use efficiency.
rows.notes: The study is a primary field trial of deficit irrigation strategies (SDI, RDI, PRD under drip) in a single orange orchard. Its result is that long-term deficit irrigation saved up to ~53% water with higher WUE and no significant loss of yield or fruit quality (Tables 5-7), which the authors frame as adaptation of the orchard to water shortage. It does not test app-based or smart irrigation scheduling: irrigation was scheduled with the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith approach adjusted by Kc and a localised factor, with soil moisture probes used for occasional corrections; no app, sensor-driven controller or decision-support tool is evaluated. The technology in the claim row (app_scheduling) therefore does not match the technology studied, so Q2 is no and Q3-Q9 follow.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study concerns deficit irrigation strategies in citrus, not app-based or smart scheduling; the review cites it under a generic 'water-saving technologies, smart irrigation' heading.
